deep.reconstruction: This page contains no mathematics. It is an archival cover or contents note, probably in a later hand: an archivist, editor or family member sorting the Nachlass, not Riemann himself. It describes the documents that follow in the bundle. Translation: 'Fair copy of a part of the draft for the disputation. The first drafts are still extant. Title for the copies of the dissertation intended for distribution. Latin version of the disputation.' The note refers to the formal requirements of Riemann's Göttingen doctorate. These were the inaugural dissertation 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse' (1851), its title page for the printed distribution copies, and the public disputation of Latin theses (December 1851). There are no derivations to reconstruct. The pencil '95' in the right margin is the folio number. The previous page (94v) holds only small decimal additions, unrelated to any mathematical argument: 6.39+2.52+2.38=11.29, 5.18+1.26=6.44 and 16.79+1.26=18.05. All three sums are correct.

results.what: Archival description of documents relating to Riemann's 1851 doctoral dissertation and disputation (fair copy of part of the disputation draft, title page for distribution copies, Latin version of the disputation theses)
